title: How SEGA keeps players moving at Sonic speed with Auth0
summary: By building SEGA Account on the Auth0 Platform, the gaming giant is unifying its global fans.
body_markdown:
SEGA fans, much like the renowned game developer’s iconic Blue Blur, Sonic, have a need for speed and agility. But jumping from on-the-go mobile gameplay to a competitive PC tournament to big-screen console gaming long meant navigating speed bumps: separate platform accounts, different passwords, and fragmented profiles.


It was enough to make a hedgehog lose its rings.


With tens of millions of passionate fans worldwide, SEGA understood that player experience had to come first. To make moving between platforms as effortless as a flawless speedrun, the company set out to build[SEGA Account](https://sega-account.com/) , a global login foundation designed to give fans one ID for all SEGA Group entertainment. To bring this vision to life, SEGA adopted Okta’s Auth0.

Launched in Japan in January 2025, SEGA Account has rapidly grown to support millions of users worldwide. Much more than a simple login update, this digital transformation is designed to help SEGA deepen ties with its fanbase and grow its business worldwide.


Getting to this seamless experience, however, first required untangling decades of disconnected, aging systems.


## When legacy infrastructure meets modern problems


As SEGA grew over the years, so did its structural challenges. In Japan alone, the company had built login systems across more than 30 web services. Aging and disconnected, these in-house setups struggled to keep up with modern security threats and fell behind on platform updates. The architecture also required that players create a new login ID for every single game title or web service they interacted with, moving SEGA further and further away from its vision of an integrated system.


To support future global expansion and connect their entire entertainment universe, SEGA needed a secure, flexible, and scalable way to manage player logins. Rather than rebuilding everything from scratch, SEGA chose to partner with Okta to implement Auth0, a platform that combines security with scalability. This decision set off an 18-month journey: six months of planning, three months of proof-of-concept testing, and nine months of implementation and deployment preparation.

## Game on: How Auth0 helped solve SEGA's biggest challenges


SEGA had three core needs: free up its engineering teams to focus on games, comply with global privacy laws, and better understand the people who play its games. Auth0 helped deliver on all three.


### Free engineers to build better experiences


Maintaining and operating an identity infrastructure in-house takes a lot of time and energy. By transferring critical identity operations like security updates, threat monitoring, and alerts to Okta, SEGA freed up its engineering team to focus on delivering on the company’s core values: building innovative games and organizing outstanding events.


### Simplify global compliance


Meeting different privacy laws around the world is difficult. With Auth0, SEGA implemented an automated system that detects a user's age based on their region during registration, ensuring parental or guardian consent is in place for minors. Supported by Okta, SEGA easily handles strict compliance requirements, such as the EU’s GDPR data deletion and data disclosure requests.


### Bring together player data


Before the company unveiled SEGA Account, player data existed in separate systems: mobile gameplay in one, console data in another, user surveys elsewhere. Auth0 unified all of it. Merging gameplay information with user attributes has allowed SEGA to build a multidimensional view of each user's interests, play patterns, retention rates, and purchasing behavior, helping pave the way for game experiences and marketing outreach that are tailored to a player’s actual interests.


## How unified identity is also unifying SEGA fans


The value of unifying identity under "SEGA Account" and "Auth0" is already showing results, starting with the ways SEGA brings fans together.


For example, players are currently competing in the Sonic Racing Cross Worlds World Championship 2026. The best players from around the globe are racing to reach the grand finals.


To celebrate the finals on October 9, 2026, SEGA is launching a Twitch Drops campaign for the viewing audience. By signing up for a SEGA Account and linking it to their Twitch account, fans can watch the official championship stream and unlock exclusive in-game rewards.

In the past, linking player accounts, web portals, and streaming platforms was a frustrating process that users would abandon. By using the Auth0 Platform, SEGA removed those hurdles to create a safe, simple connection between watching the action and playing the game.


*To get the latest tournament updates and learn how to link accounts, visit the official site:[Sonic Racing Cross Worlds World Championship 2026 Official Site](https://www.sega.com/ja/sonic-racing-crossworlds-world-championship-2026)*


## Looking ahead: Passwordless logins and real-world experiences


The evolution of SEGA Account does not stop here.


To make logging in even easier and more secure, SEGA is looking to implement passkeys. This next-generation authentication standard allows players to sign in without typing a password, using biometrics like fingerprints or facial recognition instead. Auth0’s extensibility means SEGA can roll out these new security tools quickly as technology changes.


Looking further ahead, SEGA envisions extending SEGA Account beyond the digital world of phones, PCs, and consoles. Their long-term goal is to connect all of their brand touchpoints—including physical retail stores, live events, and official merchandise shops—under one login. From the moment a player starts a game to the moment they buy a T-shirt, SEGA and Okta are working together to keep the experience safe, simple, and straightforward.


## A seamless future for global play


By removing yesterday’s speed bumps, SEGA has removed a barrier between players and the experiences they want. With Auth0 handling identity infrastructure securely in the background, SEGA's teams can focus on what matters: building great games and connecting global communities. For millions of players, that means less friction and more time doing what they came to do: play.
